title: Minimal Polynomial Reduction and Annihilator Theory
description: Proves that any polynomial function of a matrix can be reduced modulo the minimal polynomial: aeval M f = aeval M (f mod minpoly K M). Shows the minimal polynomial generates the annihilator ideal and gives the sharpest degree bound. Compares minpoly vs charpoly reduction: minpoly is at least as tight. Proves the nonderogatory characterization: minpoly = charpoly iff charpoly generates the annihilator ideal. 30 theorems, 0 definitions, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: The minimal polynomial is the sharpest annihilating polynomial for a matrix M. While the Cayley-Hamilton theorem says charpoly(M) annihilates M, the minimal polynomial is the smallest monic polynomial with this property. For scalar matrices (cI), minpoly = X - c has degree 1 while charpoly has degree n. The annihilator ideal {p : p(M) = 0} is exactly the principal ideal generated by minpoly — a fundamental result in linear algebra.
overview.problemStatement: Show that the minimal polynomial gives optimal polynomial reduction for matrix evaluation, provides the annihilator ideal, and characterizes nonderogatory matrices.
overview.text: For any polynomial f and n×n matrix M, aeval M f depends only on f mod minpoly(M). This is the optimal reduction: the remainder has degree < deg(minpoly) ≤ n. The ideal {p : aeval M p = 0} is principal, generated by minpoly(M). A matrix is nonderogatory (minpoly = charpoly) iff this ideal is generated by charpoly. This characterization connects to control theory: M is nonderogatory iff the associated linear system is observable/controllable.
overview.proofStrategy: Use Mathlib's Polynomial.modByMonic_add_div (division algorithm) and Matrix.aeval_self_charpoly. Prove minpoly annihilates M. Show any annihilating polynomial is divisible by minpoly. Derive the annihilator ideal characterization.
keyInsights: Minpoly annihilates M: the fundamental property used for all reductions
Division algorithm: f = q * minpoly + r, so aeval M f = aeval M r
Annihilator ideal = principal ideal by minpoly — characterizes all matrix relations
prerequisites: Polynomial arithmetic: remainder, division, degree bounds

conclusion.summary: Minimal polynomial reduction fully verified: aeval M f = aeval M (f mod minpoly), annihilator ideal = ⟨minpoly⟩, nonderogatory characterization. 30 theorems, 447 lines, 0 axioms.
conclusion.implications: The minimal polynomial reduction is used in matrix function computation, control theory (controllability), and Jordan form analysis. The annihilator ideal characterization is key to the rational canonical form and module decomposition theorems.
